hints: Compare each atomic radius with its ionic radius, and remember what happens to size when electrons are lost or gained.
V gets much smaller as an ion (0.186 to 0.095 nm) so it must have lost its outer shell, while Z gets much larger (0.099 to 0.181 nm) so it must have gained electrons.
Think about where metals that form positive ions and non-metals that form negative ions sit in Period 3, and how electronegativity changes across the period.
walkthrough:
**Use size change to identify ion type**

Think like this. Losing electrons to form a positive ion removes the outer shell, so the ion is much smaller than the atom. Gaining electrons to form a negative ion adds repulsion but keeps the shells, so the ion is larger than the atom.

For V: $0.186 \text{ nm} \rightarrow 0.095 \text{ nm}$ (smaller, so cation). For Z: $0.099 \text{ nm} \rightarrow 0.181 \text{ nm}$ (larger, so anion).

**Place V and Z in Period 3**

Both are in Period 3, so both atoms start with 3 electron shells. V forms a cation, so V must be a metal on the left side like $\text{Na}$, $\text{Mg}$ or $\text{Al}$. Z forms an anion, so Z must be a non-metal on the right side like $\text{P}$, $\text{S}$ or $\text{Cl}$.

**Apply the electronegativity trend**

Across a period from left to right, nuclear charge increases and atomic radius decreases, so attraction for bonding electrons increases. That means electronegativity increases across Period 3.

$$\text{electronegativity increases: Na < Mg < Al < Si < P < S < Cl}$$
Since Z is to the right of V, Z has the greater electronegativity.

options.A: Incorrect. V loses its whole n=3 outer shell to form e.g. $\text{Na}^{+}$ (2,8), so its ion has only 2 occupied shells. Z gains electrons but keeps all 3 shells e.g. $\text{Cl}^{-}$ (2,8,8), so its ion has 3 occupied shells. They do not have the same number.
options.B: Incorrect. The ionic radius of Z (0.181 nm) is larger than its atomic radius (0.099 nm). This size increase is characteristic of a negatively charged anion, where added electron-electron repulsion expands the electron cloud, not a positive ion.
options.C: Correct. V is a Period 3 metal (cation former, left side) and Z is a Period 3 non-metal (anion former, right side). Electronegativity increases across Period 3 from left to right, so Z on the right has greater electronegativity than V on the left.
options.D: Incorrect. Metals on the left like V have only 1 to 3 outer electrons, while non-metals on the right like Z have 5 to 7 outer electrons. So V has fewer outer electrons than Z, not more. This is the reverse of the statement.
